one_month_reasoning: No CoreWeave earnings fall inside Oct 2-31: Q2 was reported Aug 11 and Q3 2025 was reported Nov 10, 2025, so Q3 2026 most likely lands in the second week of November (judgment; date not yet confirmed). Things that can move the stock in the window: (1) supply from the new ATM program (up to 35M shares, ~6% of the float) and steady insider Form 144/Form 4 selling (CEO sold 200k shares Sep 22). That is a mild headwind. (2) Credit headlines: CDS is ~810bp and bonds yield 11-12%, so any widening hits the equity hard, as it did in July. (3) AI-capex read-throughs from hyperscaler earnings in late October, which could swing either way. (4) The FOMC meeting in late October. GPU rental indices show no stress (OCPI H100 rose from $2.71 to $2.92; Silicon Data +4.9% w/w), and the stock has bounced from $79.88 (Sep 17) to $88.57 on the JPM upgrade and UBS initiation. There is no clear edge, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal: median $88.0 (slightly below spot for ATM supply) and 1-month vol 26% (93%/3.5).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a 10-year unlevered DCF ($29/sh: WACC 12%, g 3%, 58% EBITDA margin, growth capex 2.3x incremental revenue, 32% steady-state replacement capex, $59B net debt by Oct-27, 600M shares) and 6.0x NTM EV/EBITDA on $20.4B Oct-27 NTM EBITDA ($105/sh). Thin cash returns on capital after replacement capex and heavy debt pull the DCF well below the market.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue $12.8B (2026) -> $26.3B (2027) -> $56B (2030) -> $76B (2036); EBITDA 58-59%; capex = 2.3x next-year revenue increase + replacement ramping to 32% of revenue; taxes 21% of a 20% EBIT margin from 2029; WACC 12%, g 3%; EV at Oct-27 $76.8B less net debt $59.1B = $17.7B / 600M sh. Sensitivity: WACC 11% -> $50, 13% -> $13; replacement capex 28% -> $60, 36% -> ~$0; growth capex 2.0x -> $53, 2.7x -> ~-$2.

inputs_detail.derivation: Growth decays from 44% to ~3%; 2030 ~$56B sized against mgmt target of >=8 GW active by 2030 (1.5 GW active at Q2 producing ~$10.3B run-rate revenue => ~$7M rev/MW-yr) with contracted 4.2 GW + ~1.5 GW powered land/LOIs

Q2 adj. EBITDA margin 59%; held ~flat because spot H100 indices ($2.7-3.8/hr) are flat-to-down m/m while CoreWeave's Platinum rating and July ~25% list price rise support premium; slight fade for re-contracting older fleets at lower rates

2026 capex guide $35-39B vs consensus 2027 revenue increase ~$13.5B => 2.7x; 2025 PP&E capex $10.3B vs 2026 revenue increase ~$7.7B => 1.3x; part of 2026 capex is CIP ($11.9B) for 2028 revenue, so 2.3x used
6-yr GPU depreciation life implies replacing 2.3/6 = 38% of revenue/yr; re-contracting of prior-gen GPUs at 'at or above' prior prices (call) extends economic life to ~7 yrs => ~32%

inputs_detail.value: 0% through 2028 (NOLs), then 21% of EBIT at 20% EBIT margin
inputs_detail.derivation: GAAP losses (FY25 net loss $1.17B, H1'26 $1.37B) build NOLs; adj. operating margin 5% in Q2 guided to low teens in Q4; steady-state EBIT margin 20% judged from D&A ~38% of revenue

Roughly nominal GDP / below the 5.3% 10y yield; growth capex at 2.3x still charged in terminal year

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) adj. EBITDA $20.4B x 6.0x = $122.4B EV less net debt $59.1B = $63.3B / 600M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.25 x 2027 EBITDA $15.5B (59% x $26.3B consensus revenue) + 0.75 x 2028 EBITDA $22.0B (58% x $38B)

Market today: equity $48.8B (551.5M x $88.57) + est. net debt ~$40B (Jun-30 $28.65B + Q3 burn ~$11B and $4.2B convert) = ~$89B EV on NTM EBITDA ~$14B => ~6.4x; trimmed to 6.0x as revenue growth decelerates from ~105% to ~44%

bear.story: The AI-capex cycle 'self-throttles' as credit tightens: CDS widens past the July ~855bp peak, DDTL draw conditions force more equity (ATM fully used plus more), spot GPU pricing keeps sliding (H100 ~$2.7/hr) and short 3-6 month contracts reprice lower. A top customer (36%/26%/10% concentration) slows new orders as it builds in-house capacity. EV/EBITDA compresses to ~4.5x on ~$18B NTM EBITDA against ~$62B net debt and ~620M shares.

base.story: Execution roughly on consensus: ~$26B 2027 revenue, ~59% EBITDA margin, active power rising toward 3 GW, and backlog (>$129B incl. Q3 adds) converting. Net debt still climbs to ~$59B and the ATM dilutes ~6%. The market keeps paying ~6x NTM EBITDA, so the stock roughly holds, with EBITDA growth offset by debt growth and dilution.

bull.story: Demand for Vera Rubin/Blackwell stays sold out, the July ~25% price increase and premium short-dated contracts lift margins (5-10pt higher contribution margins), CDS tightens toward IG-adjacent levels, and 2027 revenue beats ($28-30B). The multiple re-rates to ~7.5x NTM EBITDA (~$22B), with sell-side targets (avg $141.58) acting as the anchor. Converts start to become convertible above ~$127.

thesis_break_reason: $45 is ~25% below the 52-week low of $60.55 (set in the July CDS scare) and roughly where the equity would sit if EV/EBITDA fell to ~5x with net debt at ~$45-50B. A sustained trade there would most likely mean the financing machine has stalled (a failed or very expensive debt raise, CDS well beyond 900bp, a covenant or draw-condition problem on the DDTLs) or a top customer has cut or deferred commitments. That would be a fundamental problem, not ordinary volatility for a 93%-vol stock.

reasoning: Facts: Q2'26 revenue $2.58B (+112%), adj. EBITDA 59%, adj. op margin 5%, net loss $626M, capex $9.4B. FY26 guide: revenue $12.4-13.2B, capex $35-39B. Backlog $104B plus >$25B added in Q3. Debt $35.55B against $6.9B cash at Jun-30, plus a $4.2B convert in September and a 35M-share ATM. Shares outstanding 551.5M. Alternative-lane evidence: GPU rental indices (Ornn, Silicon Data, Mercatus, AIMultiple) show H100 spot at $2.7-3.8/hr, roughly flat over the last month with a small uptick last week. That does not confirm a broad pricing boom, but there is no collapse either; CoreWeave's sole-Platinum SemiAnalysis rating supports a premium. Independent Substacks (Cape Fear, Damsker, Electron Economics, Tech Cache) focus on the funding gap between capex and committed facilities, the duration mismatch (15-year leases vs 3-year contracts), and customers turning into competitors. Credit markets agree: CDS ~811-855bp, ~50% implied 5-year default. Retail sentiment is lukewarm-to-bearish with mentions fading (AltIndex 40/100; ApeWisdom 57% positive on a tiny sample), and ARK and small newsletter buyers stepped in after the September selloff. Hiring stays robust (311 open roles, mostly engineering and data-center), which does not point to a pullback. Valuation: the DCF Kilian asked for gives ~$29 because, after replacement capex, unlevered FCF margins are only ~15% and net debt reaches ~$59B by Oct-27. A market-style 6x NTM EBITDA gives ~$105. The 50/50 blend is $67, below spot. Distribution: a 90/10 mixture of lognormals (core median $84, sigma 0.72, slightly below the 93% realized vol; distress component median $25, reflecting credit-implied default risk). That gives a median ~$76, P(>=$89) ~42%, P(>=$155) ~18%. It leans bearish against spot because of the fair-value gap, dilution and credit overhang, tempered by strong backlog and demand signals. Research limits: X posts were blocked (402), the Reddit API did not respond, and Twelve Data fundamentals and estimates required a higher plan, so I used SEC XBRL and company filings directly.
